claims.claim: Original Google Chinese BERT generally tokenizes Chinese characters individually; this does not automatically supply whole-word segmentation boundaries.
claims.verification_note: Scope qualified for mixed-language and checkpoint-specific tokenization.

claims.claim: HFL Chinese-BERT-wwm applies external Chinese word segmentation and selects all characters in a selected word as MLM targets.
claims.locator: README 简介 and WWM examples
claims.verification_note: README discusses LTP word segmentation and broad notion of masking.

claims.claim: Whole word masking changes the MLM target grouping, while original token labels remain individual token IDs.
claims.verification_note: Teaching cross-entropy formula averages over selected valid token positions.

claims.claim: MacBERT changes MLM to correction with similar-word replacement on 80 percent of selected positions, 10 percent random and 10 percent unchanged.
claims.verification_note: Do not conflate with original BERT 80 percent [MASK] replacement.

claims.claim: Baidu ERNIE 2019 includes phrase-level and entity-level knowledge-related masking.
claims.verification_note: Specifically refers to Sun et al. ERNIE 2019, not every model named ERNIE.

claims.claim: ACL 2021 ChineseBERT adds character glyph and pinyin representations to its input.
claims.verification_note: Distinct architecture/model from Google Chinese BERT and HFL BERT-wwm.

claims.claim: Whole word masking benefits vary by task, illustrated by findings on Chinese grammatical error correction.
claims.verification_note: Rejects unconditional claim that WWM improves all Chinese tasks.
